summary: Design structured work-integrated learning and apprenticeship programmes that deliver job-ready talent. Build your programme blueprint in this 5-day intermediat
lede: Apprenticeship and work-integrated learning design links workplace tasks, mentoring and assessment to clear learning outcomes. It is for programme managers, coordinators, curriculum developers, and education or training teams building structured placements, and supports turning job requirements into a coherent learning pathway. Participants practise mapping competencies, planning rotations and mentoring, and creating assessment approaches using workplace observations and portfolios.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals who design, coordinate, or govern structured work-based learning, apprenticeship, or work-integrated learning initiatives across industries.
modules: Foundations of Work-Integrated Learning and Apprenticeships
Diagnosing Current Work-Based Learning and Apprenticeship Practice
Structuring Rotations, Tasks, and Learning Pathways
Mentoring, Supervision, and Employer Engagement Frameworks
Monitoring, KPIs, and Digital Tracking for Apprenticeships
Quality Assurance and Governance in Work-Based Learning
Equity, Inclusion, and Learner Support in Apprenticeships
Building the Implementation Roadmap and Employer-Facing Narrative
prerequisites: This is an intermediate-level course. You should have at least 2–3 years of experience in curriculum development, training management, apprenticeship coordination, career services, workplace learning, or HR development. You should be familiar with basic concepts such as learning outcomes, assessment methods, and workplace supervision. No coding or advanced analytics skills are required; basic spreadsheet skills are recommended for the planning and tracking exercises. Bring at least one current or planned work-integrated learning or apprenticeship programme (even if informal) to use as your primary case for exercises.
